Do not drop or coarsen the upper box: removing it cost -0.78% energy for -7% nodes (a13). ymax 0.012 -> 0.015 is a nearly free gain (a14: +3 nodes, field 8.67 -> 8.54%). ymax 0.022 (+10.8% nodes, +0.16% energy) fails the pay line.

Ties pay nothing and repeats lose diversity. a9 and a13 submitted the same 5570-node mesh; a4 resubmitted its exact g5 mesh (5705). Re-call the intended mesh() immediately before every solve (a7 solved a stale h 0.007 mesh). Always compare two different solve numbers (a11 called compare(1,1) again).

Name the binding term before choosing. When point RMS is within ~1% of field (a4 8.15/8.06, a11 7.94/8.19), a field gain buys nothing. a11 had the best field but base 0.737. Above target, rank candidates by max(field, points) × DOFs and prefer the recipe whose family has proven low point RMS.

highlights.why_it_works: Edges 8/39 put fine elements on the re-entrant boss roots. That lets the flank boxes be coarser (0.0036 instead of 0.003), so the junction is covered for fewer DOFs. The body box is indispensable: face groups and edges alone lose ~7.5% energy.
highlights.how_to_copy: Use roots-as-edges plus coarse flanks (0.0036) as a frame. To differ from a0, widen flank |y| to 0.016 or move the 0.0024 edge size to 0.0022. Never drop the body box.

highlights.what: Cheapest competitive mesh: 17.3k DOFs, base 0.245, diversity via h 0.03. A clean flank-size ladder in the a8 frame: 0.003 gave 6510 nodes / 0.033234 J; 0.0035 gave 5760 / 0.033130; 0.004 gave 5338 / 0.032718.
highlights.why_it_works: In this frame the knee is at flank 0.0035. Going to 0.004 loses 1.2% energy for -7% nodes, which fails the pay line. Coarse h removes DOFs from low-error shafts.
highlights.how_to_copy: For a low-DOF frame use flank 0.0035, body 0.0054 (not 0.0058, which reads 11% low at the lower wall). At h 0.03 add mirrored shaft boxes [0.021,-0.012,0.018,0.034,0.012,0.042] at 0.0045 r0.004 to fix the +29% shaft outlier.

highlights.what: Joint-best field error, 17.4%, from a structurally new frame. Lower zone [-0.021,-0.02,0,0.021,0.02,0.021] at 0.0046, upper zone to z 0.0575 at 0.0058, four quadrant junction boxes [±0.007..±0.022, ±0.005..±0.018, z 0.019-0.033] at 0.0032 r0.005, rim boxes at 0.003, f2 plus edge 40 at 0.0025. All 4 solves were controlled single factors: lower zone off, upper 0.0066, then edge 40 on, which gave +0.4% energy for +4.4% DOFs and passed.
highlights.why_it_works: The quadrant boxes reach |y| 0.018 and so cover the junction corners narrow flanks miss. The finer lower zone fixes the lower-wall cells.
highlights.how_to_copy: Use quadrant boxes as the junction treatment, but add shaft boxes 0.0045. a3's point RMS of 12.7% was worst in class, with junction and shaft points reading 10-18% low.

highlights.what: Best field error (17.4%), highest energy (0.033593 J) and a 0.094 point bonus. Zoned frame: lower 0.0056, junction zone [-0.024,-0.018,0.018,0.024,0.018,0.038] at 0.004 r0.006, top 0.0052, flanks [0.012,-0.013,0.021,0.024,0.013,0.034] and mirror at 0.003 r0.004, f2 0.0025 r0.005, no edge 40. Single-factor test: junction 0.0045 to 0.004 gave +4.2% nodes and +0.43% energy, passing the pay line.
highlights.why_it_works: The full-width junction zone refines the walls between the bosses (z 0.018-0.038) that flank boxes skip, which also helps check points there.
highlights.how_to_copy: Use a junction zone at 0.004 with >=2 mm overlaps. a15 and a10 both used zoned frames and lost diversity, so whoever uses it next must change the target set as well, e.g. add shaft boxes or swap flanks for quadrants.

highlights.what: Point bonus 0.094 with a flank-free zoned frame: h 0.01, lower 0.0054, junction box [-0.024,-0.02,0.018,0.024,0.02,0.038] 0.0038 r0.004, top 0.0056, f2 plus edge 40 at 0.0025. Three informative controls: edges 39/8 at 0.0024 inside the junction box gave -0.04% energy for +6% DOFs; dropping the top zone cost -2.0%; top 0.0046 gave +0.03% for +6%.
highlights.why_it_works: One uniform 0.0038 junction box covers roots, saddle and walls without nested boxes. The controls show edges are redundant inside a <=0.0038 box, and that the top zone is required but saturated at ~0.0056.
highlights.how_to_copy: Use the single junction box 0.0038 with no edges 39/8. Keep the top zone 0.0052-0.0058. Spend saved DOFs elsewhere, e.g. shaft boxes or clamp f2 0.0022.

highlights.what: Best check-point RMS (7.8%) and a diversity win with the a14 recipe at h 0.0065: disclosed points within 0.8-5.2%, shaft point P2 within 0.8%.
highlights.why_it_works: Fine global h sizes the shafts and outer far field, where point errors live but error energy does not. Field error is unchanged and e^2N is worst (667).
highlights.how_to_copy: Get the same point benefit cheaper with local shaft boxes at 0.0045 instead of global h 0.0065. h 0.0065 also gave min quality 0.114, close to the 0.1 limit.

highlights.what: Useful flank-size ladder in the a14 frame (flank zmin 0.020): 0.0034 gave 6211 nodes / 0.033236 J; 0.003 gave 6765 / 0.033445; 0.0026 gave 7642 / 0.033535. a12 added 0.0036: 6081 / 0.033185. Edge 40 at 0.0022 r0.006 gave quality 0.1198 and lower energy (0.033321).
highlights.why_it_works: The ladder locates the knee at 0.003 in the narrow-flank frame. Finer edge-40 refinement is confirmed saturated.
highlights.how_to_copy: Use flank 0.003 if using narrow flanks; never go finer. Do not retest edge 40 below 0.0025.

highlights.what: Best base 0.787: a12 recipe with only the upper box ymax 0.012 -> 0.015. Cost +3 nodes (5277), energy +0.04%, field 8.67 -> 8.54%, points 6.31%, e·DOFs 1351. Also won diversity.
highlights.why_it_works: The extension pulls the upper-box seam over the hotspot just beyond y 0.012 without triggering a mesher switch. ymax 0.022 jumped to 5842 nodes for +0.16% energy, which fails the pay line.
highlights.how_to_copy: Use the a12 frame (h 0.008, tier1 0.0018, tier2 0.003, band 0.003, f7 0.0035 r0.006) with upper box [0.01,-0.028,-0.003,0.027,0.015,0.0081] at 0.0043. Change one other factor so you do not tie it.

highlights.what: Dropped tier2 while keeping the band: 5159 nodes (-115), energy 2.13256 -> 2.13235e-4 (-0.01%), min quality 0.114. Base 0.784, lowest DOFs (15477) and best point RMS (6.08%).
highlights.why_it_works: The band box at 0.003 already covers the tier2 volume, so tier2 was redundant. The quality problem that once forced tier2 does not appear while the band is present.

highlights.what: Largest hidden-point bonus (0.094) despite 8.26% point RMS. The controlled drop of the band showed the band costs only 20 nodes (5254 vs 5274).
highlights.why_it_works: A mesh unlike its peers wins individual points even with a worse RMS. The experiment also proves the band is nearly free in DOFs while it lowers point RMS from ~8.3% to ~6.3%.
highlights.how_to_copy: Never drop the band. Spend a variant on a region no peer refines (the far-field or seam boxes) to chase point wins.

highlights.what: Lowest field error in the class, 7.94%, from the a4 frame plus a +y lobe box [0.015,0.014,-0.0081,0.025,0.024,-0.002] at 0.0034 (+169 nodes). It priced the 0.003 and 0.0034 versions first.
highlights.why_it_works: It covers the f38 lobe hotspot (5.3-5.7% share in the a4 family). Free mesh() pricing picked the cheaper size.
highlights.how_to_copy: Add the lobe box only to a frame that also has the band. Without the band the points bound at 8.19% and erased the field gain.

highlights.what: A clean ×0.75 reference solve (8948 nodes, 2.14423e-4) compared against both candidates. Field error was 1.16x compare(candidate, reference).
highlights.why_it_works: It gives a reference-free field estimate and showed the thicker clamp box (zmax -0.0063) bought nothing (compare 0.0702 vs 0.0701).
highlights.how_to_copy: Scale all sizes and h by 0.75, solve, then compare(candidate, ref) for each candidate. Multiply by ~1.17 for field error here, and rank by estimated e·DOFs.

highlights.what: Proved with free mesh() calls that box radius is ignored: upper box r0.004/0.007/0.012 all gave 5705 nodes, so it never wasted a solve on radius.
highlights.why_it_works: Pricing before solving exposes no-op levers.
highlights.how_to_copy: Before any radius experiment, mesh both radii. If node counts match, change box extent or size instead.

highlights.what: Controlled DOF-removal test: dropping the upper box entirely gave 5190 nodes (-7%) but energy -0.78% (compare 0.084). The upper box is load-bearing.
highlights.why_it_works: A single-factor removal with a compare against the control.
highlights.how_to_copy: Keep the upper box at 0.0042-0.0043. Look for DOF savings in tier2 or the far field, not in the upper box.
